findings.title: getForLogin loses the delegate's deterministic ordering
findings.body: The cached path collects identity-provider IDs into a Set and then builds a HashSet<IdentityProviderModel> (lines 244-254) before returning identityProviders.stream(). This discards the ordering of idpDelegate.getForLogin(), which concatenates realm-level providers before organization providers and otherwise follows the storage query order. Callers of getForLogin that do not explicitly sort (the login bean does, but other broker/manager callers may not) will now observe arbitrary, potentially call-varying ordering instead of the previous deterministic order.

findings.title: New getLoginPredicate clause can NPE on a null config map
findings.body: getLoginPredicate() now evaluates Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) for every identity provider whose organizationId is non-null, without checking getConfig() for null. IdentityProviderModel config is settable and can be null for models built from representations or by custom code. Previously the predicate only called isEnabled/isLinkOnly/isHideOnLogin and could not fail this way. In the new cache code this predicate is invoked from create/update/remove in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider before the delegate operation runs, so a null-config organization-linked IdP would fail creation/update/removal with an NPE instead of being processed.

findings.title: Login cache aggregates an unbounded entry per organization under three keys
findings.body: cacheKeyForLogin creates only one cache key per FetchMode, while organizationId is stored as the searchKey inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery. Every distinct organizationId first seen for a mode therefore goes through the miss branch (lines 233-241), invalidates the whole shared object, and re-adds a new query copied from the previous one. In realms with many organizations this creates one retained ID set per organization ever queried under REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL, makes adding each new organization copy all previously cached variants, and means the REALM_ONLY cache also accumulates spurious per-organization entries even though that mode ignores organizationId. This is unbounded cache growth and invalidation churn proportional to the number of organizations.

findings.title: New login-cache test cleans up a literal alias and never asserts cache-hit results
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") instead of the created alias (idp-alias-<i>, and similarly idp-alias-20 at line 425), so the 21 created providers are not removed by cleanup and removal of the non-existent alias 'alias' may itself error during cleanup. Additionally, the test only asserts IdentityProviderListQuery sizes inside the cache; it never calls getForLogin a second time and asserts the aliases actually returned on a cache hit, so defects in the cached reconstruction path (for example wrong/missing providers returned via getById) would not be caught.
